==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|covenaunt}} {{qualifier|obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|covenaunt}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|covenant||agreement}}, from {{der|en|la|conveniens|conveniēns, convenientem|agreeing, [[agreeable]], suitable, convenient}}, present participle of {{m|la|conveniō||to agree}}. Cognate with {{m|en|convenient}} and {{m|en|convene}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌv.ən.ənt/|/ˈkʌv.nənt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-covenant.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌvənənt|ʌvnənt|s1=3|s2=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|legal}} An [[agreement]] to do or not do a [[particular]] thing.
# {{lb|en|legal}} A [[promise]], [[incidental]] to a [[deed]] or [[contract]], either [[express]] or [[implied]].
# A [[pact]] or [[binding]] [[agreement]] between two or more parties (often one that is religious or religiously-based).
# An [[incidental]] clause in an agreement.

====Synonyms====
* [[Thesaurus:pact]]
* [[Thesaurus:agreement]]

{{en-verb}}

# To enter into, or promise something by, a covenant.
#* {{RQ:L'Estrange Fables of Aesop|passage=Jupiter '''Covenanted''' with him, that it should be Hot or Cold, Wet or Dry, {{...}} as the Tenant should Direct.}}

# {{lb|en|legal}} To [[bind]] oneself in [[contract]].
# {{lb|en|legal}} To make a [[stipulation]].
